newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds flat after rally, ignore IBCA.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds flat after rally, ignore IBCA.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat late morning Thursday as the market paused after the breakneck pace of gains in recent days.
"Its quiet now. The market is taking a rest after the gains," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 93, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.05 at 122.85.

The market did not pay much attention to news by IBCA, the European credit rating agency, that it had assigned a BB rating to Argentina's medium- and long-term debt even though the agency said the rating outlook was "positive."
The "positive" outlook makes the rating higher than Standard & Poor's which has Argentina at BB but with only a "stable" outlook.
"It (the IBCA news) is important but I do not think it will move the market," said another trader.
